question.text:

For x > 0, which solution of y + y/x = cos x has a finite limit as x → 0 ?
(A) sin x + cos x/x (B) sin x + (cos x − 1)/x
(C) cos x + (sin x − 1)/x (D) sin x + 1/x
(E) cos x

solution.text:
′
Multiplication by x gives (xy) = x cos x. Integrating yields xy = x sin x + cos x + C. A finite
limit at zero requires C = −1, canceling the constant numerator. The remaining expression
tends to 0.
